name: Dual Littlestone Dimension of Half-intervals
details: Endpoint rounding depends on whether the empty and full threshold are included.
proof: The dual of the $n$ half-intervals is the class of terminal segments on an $n$-element ordered domain. A balanced binary-search tree on its endpoints gives depth $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor$, while a depth-d shattered tree needs $2^d$ distinct terminal segments. Thus its Littlestone dimension, and hence $\mathrm L^*(\mathcal I_n)$, is $\Theta(\log_2n)$.
references: Direct dualization of the standard threshold-tree calculation in \cite{littlestone1988learning}.
